prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: landscape 16:9 editorial image for the "Der Anschluss" card on the German AImation engineering consultancy website.
Primary request: AI-assisted OFFICE WORK and document automation, not manufacturing. A plausible contemporary product-development office, seen in a close three-quarter over-the-shoulder view. One casually dressed adult engineer sits at a real desk, reviewing a document on a single large desktop monitor. Focus on the monitor and normal office work, not the person's face. A slim keyboard, mouse and one open notebook, physically plausible cables and monitor stand.
On the monitor: a restrained, believable unbranded desktop application. A simple document workflow occupies the upper portion of the actual screen, three connected steps with the exact short German labels "Eingang", "Entwurf", "Prüfung". Below it are an incoming document list and a neatly structured draft report being reviewed. One small application heading "KI-Assistent". Only these few readable labels, no fake dense text. The workflow is contained inside the screen, never floating in the air. The engineer's relaxed hand rests naturally on the mouse.
Style: premium documentary editorial photography, realistically imperfect matte desk textures, ordinary natural daylight from a window, graphite and warm neutral palette consistent with a dark engineering website, readable shadows, restrained saturation, 50mm lens. Main subject inside central 75% for thumbnail cropping, visual clarity at small size. Background softly out of focus, modest modern office.
Avoid: conveyor belts, factories, machinery, industrial robots, metal parts, server rooms, holograms, floating icons, glowing brains, sci-fi lighting, neon, staged smiling teams, luxury offices, marketing text, logos, watermarks, impossible hardware, extra hands. Do not include a KI-generiert label inside the image; the website adds that separately.
review: Replaces the production conveyor with an office document workflow and human review. Fictional interface, not a product screenshot. Previous asset retained.
typography: Removed reporting-only size/weight override; all six .pain-title elements use the same responsive typography.
